items.title: Harold Danko interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 28, 2021
items.q: Somebody just sent me, I went to Brazil with Anita O’Day and somebody just sent me an audio of it.

ctx.x: Sure. Absolutely yeah that was part of the fun for me. At the beginning I was not a very good transposer. You know if I knew that I had to do it I would write out a quick lead sheet or at least the chords in other keys. But then it got to be where most of the tunes I knew well enough, especially if there was a chart I mean it was not a problem. But I remember one night with Liza there was an intro, I gave her a D7 and we used to just — because she could be very spontaneous and funny. But the show was very…

winging it. You know she was taking a slight liberty, and thank goodness I knew the tune. You know. But I mean most singers had charts and it would be, I remember Anita O’Day was a bit difficult because she would do verses and really just run right through the verse. And I wouldn’t have the words, it would be a tune I didn’t know the words to the verse. And she’d have like somebody had done a lead sheet with the melody but that’s not what she did. She was just running right through it to get to whatever it was.…
Playing for singers, did that bear fruit when you started playing for Chet Baker and Lee Konitz? They’re both such great melodists.
